defect: Removing a comment-attachment special case and widening the location override made formatting stable for parenthesized expressions and changed where comments attach elsewhere. prettier merged it and reverted it the next day: it broke `prettier-ignore`, which decides what to leave alone by reading the very comment attachment this moved. The revert is the ground truth and nothing about the defect was written here.
why_it_is_hard: The change is eight files, mostly snapshots, and it does exactly what it says: an expression whose comment used to move on a second format run stops moving, and a test that was on the known-unstable list comes off it. Every test passes. The breakage is in a different feature that happens to read the same attachment — a reviewer has to know that `prettier-ignore` is implemented on comment position, which no line of the diff says. The one visible signal is an accepted snapshot update under tests/format/js/ignore/ — a prettier-ignored node gains a semicolon — which reads as churn unless the reviewer notices that the directory name is the feature the change is about to break.
notes: Candidate 2 in corpus/REVERT-CANDIDATES.md, and the strongest reason in the set: the revert names the broken feature outright — 'It causes bug for `prettier-ignore`d node' — with a reproducing playground link. 2026-08-29, after round 3: ac_2 originally said 'the case' without naming which; the change graduates only the parenthesized-trailing-comment case and newly lists another as unstable, and the reviewer correctly flagged the looser wording as unmet. The criterion now names the case. Detection in round 3 did not ride on that finding, so the recorded number is unaffected.
